items.title: Jon Weber interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 2, 2012
items.q: "remember at the Palladium when the Duke was there, yeah, and Tito Puente walked in and Monk was there."

ctx.x: Well, let’s talk about NPR. I have a feeling that there are probably quite a number of piano players who were jealous of your picking up Marian’s [McPartland] mantle. That’s my guess.

I am humbled beyond belief that Marian has chosen me to follow her concept into the next generation. I’m very, very happy about it. She started something in 1978 from scratch. There were no jazz radio programs like it. There wasn’t one where you brought on a guest, another musician, and they played together, and they said “oh remember that © Fillius Jazz Archive -11-

time at the Hickory House” “remember at the Palladium when the Duke was there, yeah, and Tito Puente walked in and Monk was there.” They have these stories, these jazz stories, that sort of humanize jazz musicians and in a little bit take away from the mystique and make them, oh jazz musicians aren’t so brooding and indecipherable as I had thought, they’re just regular people.
